thread.title: Mayor and DEGC award $300,000 in grants to 13 startups through Detroit Startup Fund
thread.title_full: Mayor and DEGC award $300,000 in grants to 13 startups through Detroit Startup Fund

author: N. R. Altamirano
title: Mayor and DEGC award $300,000 in grants to 13 startups through Detroit Startup Fund
text:
Mayor Mary Sheffield and the Detroit Economic Growth Corporation (DEGC) announced on Mar. 25 that thirteen startup companies have been selected for investment through the second round of the Detroit Startup Fund. The fund awarded ten seed grants of $15,000 each and three scale grants of $50,000 each to support high-growth businesses working on solutions in healthcare, fintech, environmental technology, advanced manufacturing, and mobility.
The initiative aims to help entrepreneurs address real-world challenges while strengthening Detroit’s reputation as a growing hub for innovation. Hundreds of applications were received for this round, showing increasing demand for early-stage capital among local founders.
“Detroit’s future is being built by entrepreneurs who are solving real problems and creating real opportunity,” said Sheffield. “The Detroit Startup Fund ensures those founders have access to the capital and support they need to grow right here in our city.”
Applicants were evaluated based on their business traction, job creation potential, scalability, and commitment to building in Detroit. Scale grant recipients included HAAS Alert for its connected vehicle safety platform; Total Analysis for rapid infectious disease testing technology; and Constrat for an AI-powered platform supporting contractors with financial tools.
“Detroit startups have the potential to once again revolutionize industries and create jobs for generations of Detroiters,” said Justin Onwenu, Director of the Office of Small Business Affairs. “Founders are choosing to build and scale their innovative startups in Detroit as part of a strong and expanding ecosystem and we are excited to support their work.”
Seed grant recipients represented a range of sectors including mobility solutions (Bhadala), civic engagement (POGO), clean energy (Electric Outdoors), education technology (EdLoop), small business support (Shophand), workforce intelligence (Ciyfr), advanced textiles (Reyz), digital resource platforms (RoundHere.io), micromobility logistics (Penny Pickup) as well as Spanish S.W.A.G., which provides interactive Spanish language learning tools developed by Jessie Feliz after participating in Motor City Match.
Kevin Johnson, DEGC President and CEO said: “The volume and quality of applications this round make clear that the pipeline is strong and growing. Through the Detroit Startup Fund, we are connecting that talent to the capital and support needed to turn ideas into scalable companies.”
Future rounds will depend on City Council approval for additional funding. The DEGC continues its mission as a non-profit organization focused on inclusive development by supporting business retention, attraction initiatives, small businesses growth projects across neighborhood commercial corridors.
